facts.says: The Obligator is a huge, dark grey spiked mace head, glowing green through the openings in its shell, on the end of a long, twisted brown vine.
The Obligator takes both hands and a lot of attack training; it can thrust out to hit several foes at once, or swing quicker at just one.
The Obligator is fed with ascension shards and nature and death runes, and it can only change hands once it's been emptied.
The Obligator is the rarest of the archive's big prizes.
Ascension crossbows are a matched pair of old crystal crossbows in sea-green and teal, one held in each hand.
The two ascension crossbows take turns, one then the other, firing faster than any ordinary crossbow but over a shorter reach.
Ascension crossbows will only take ascension bolts, chiselled from the archive's crystal shards and sometimes tipped with diamond or onyx.
Zorya's tome is a big open book with a brown cover, gold-capped corners and a long green ribbon, carried open in both arms.
Zorya's tome is weighed down by all the knowledge in it, and it casts its own spell, paid for in astral and nature runes.
The rondache is a round shield of pale silver, banded in gold and blue around a dark centre set with a gold four-pointed star.
The rondache is an old icyene shield; the blows it soaks up build a charge it can let loose in a shield slam.
The rondache is a finely made shield, and only someone with a good deal of defence training can carry it.
The living record is a cape that once honoured Guthix's archivists and is now given to those who keep defending their work.
A living record's engraving shows how often its wearer has defended the archive: Scrivener for a hundred times, then Salvager, Prospector, Reliquist and finally Antisqüien for two thousand.
The plainest living record is a pale green cape; the highest is mossy green with a skull face at the top and ragged purple-edged tails.
The first living record is claimed from a records room at the south end of the archive, behind a strange door opened with a key of stone and vines.
The archivist's folio is a green-bound book with a pale skull on the cover and branching lines spreading out round it; when it's charged, the skull's eyes glow bright green.
Guthix's archivists carried folios of manuscripts to get about, and a charged one takes its owner straight back to the archive's lobby.
The Horn of Bran is a long, curved horn, open at the wide end, brown along its length with a pale zigzag-edged band round the mouth and a pale tip.
The Horn of Bran is inscribed with the name Bran and a small symbol like the one the Knights of the Round Table wear.
King Arthur's knights count Bran's horn as one of their own, and the sight of it set them all exclaiming; Sir Tristram cheered that they'd finally get some proper ale.
Whoever brings the Horn of Bran to Camelot gets King Arthur's blessing, and with it a prayer stronger than Piety.
The Horn of Bran is one of the prizes in the archive's reward chests.
The archive gives up four fragments, of whispering wind, deep water, living earth and burning fire, and breaking one makes that element's spells hit harder for good.
The fragment of burning fire is a red flame inside a broken, spiky ring of pale brown, set round with orange four-pointed stars.
Ascension shards are bits of powerful crystal, dug from rocks in the archive's lobby or found in the raid, and used for bolts and to charge the Obligator and the folio.
Orion is a small hunched figure with a pale, bony head and long red tendrils hanging from its face, red clawed hands and a long mauve robe; one look wraps him in a dark purple hooded cloak.
Orion is a much smaller version of Ocellus, the guardian who turned on everyone in the archive's inner vault.
Reality trembles just from Orion being there.
Orion mutters that Guthix wanted balance through death and annihilation, and can be shut up with a promise of ascension juice.
Orion shouts about ascension when he's picked up.
Orion comes to people who finish the archive's raid; anyone with full hands and a full pack when he turns up can claim him from Probita in East Ardougne.
Followers of Guthix built the archive at the bottom of the Chasm of Tears to hold his knowledge and treasures.
The archive is a cache of Guthix's most prized possessions.
Work on the archive was dropped unfinished when something more urgent needed every resource; the skeleton of a Guthixian outside still holds the note saying so.

A guardian Guthix left to defend the archive lay dormant there, but it couldn't tell friend from foe, so the adventurers working with the alliance had to destroy it to take the central chamber, the Nexus.
The archive's way in opened after Lucien took the Stone of Jas from the old Guthixian temple close by.
Followers of Lucien, Zamorak and Bandos have all come to loot the archive, and the Dagon'hai, who have broken with Lucien, want it for themselves.
The archive is defended by an alliance of the Temple Knights under Eva Cashien, the Guardians of Armadyl under Armacus Selles, and Crux Eqal, whose druid Ivy Sophista brought the adventurer in.
The archive has an inner vault, and the alliance fears what's in it could be as mighty as the Stone of Jas.
Six side chambers open off the Nexus, and the alliance expects every one of them to come under attack.
Ocellus, a Guardian of Guthix charged with guarding the vault, decided nobody but Guthix was worthy of its broken blade and tried to take Guthix's place himself.
Ivy Sophista doubts Ocellus is really dead, since Guthix himself gave him his power, and he keeps trying to claim the Blade.
Crux Eqal hands down the names of guardians Guthix set over places of power after the God Wars: Juna, Valluta, Aeternam, and Ocellus, called the Guardian of Ascension.
The Blade was once Guthix's own; it hangs broken from a vine in the inner vault, still giving off power, and seems able to move by itself.

The inner vault's plinths hold odd relics: a lifelike mask that seems to move, a lantern still alight with what look like Fremennik symbols, chainlinks made to hold something big, a casing for a lighthouse lens, and an anchor whose gems bear what look like law, chaos and death symbols.
The repaired Blade carries the defenders to an otherworldly room ringed with chests, where they collect their rewards.
The way in is an opening near the old Guthixian temple at the very bottom of the Chasm of Tears, reached by riding a light creature down with a lit sapphire lantern.
The alliance cleared the cavern in front of the entrance into a camp, with a bank, a grouping board, the alliance records, a strategy board and crystal rocks to mine.
Roots wrap the crystal rocks in the lobby as if trying to keep them contained; a worked-out rock sinks into the ground and others nearby come up.
Ezekiel is a Saradominist justiciar who came for artefacts worthy of Saradomin, called anyone in his way a servant of evil, and wouldn't be talked round.
Bork is a huge Bandosian ork, once a captive of the Dagon'hai, who goes about drumming with a little goblin crew, the Smorks, working a cannon.
Bork's goblins broke into the archive's supply room and took the brooms and hammers there for artefacts of power.
Zamorakian mages used the archive's magic to try to bring the long-banished demon Dreadnoth back; they only got part of him through, and sealed what they had in jelly to keep it together.
Xarth is a tormented demon that has long mastered the eternal burning that most of its kind struggle with.
Moia, a necromancer, leads Lucien's forces at the archive, and the alliance knows little else about her.
General Montoya, an officer of the Guardians of Armadyl, stands by the strategy board in the lobby, organising people to the alliance's defence plans and bringing newcomers up to speed.
Montoya's plan is to take the Nexus first, then send troops to the far chambers while the alliance clears one side and the adventurers clear the other.
Montoya's scouts tell of a lone knight who wiped out a whole squad by himself; only one scout made it back, badly hurt.
Montoya says the Bandos forces are mostly goblins, but they've built some kind of siege engine and follow a huge ork.
Montoya's people saw an army of skeletons fighting Zamorakian mages in the deep tunnels, and a captured mage let slip they're trying to summon a demon.
Montoya heard of a tormented demon in full control of its flames that the Dagon'hai were fending off near where the Stone of Jas used to sit.
Montoya finds Armacus a bit eccentric but a fine leader and a good judge of character.
General Montoya looks left-handed.
The archive's banker travels with the alliance as its go-between with the Bank of Gielinor, so everyone has their things wherever they end up.
The archive's banker likes seeing the world but wishes the alliance's destinations weren't so often dangerous.
The archive's banker passes the quiet hours reading a book of poems thought to date from the Second Age.
The archive's banker finds there's only so much admiring of a cavern a person can do, even one this grand.
The Record Keeper insists he is THE keeper of the records, holding the archive's secrets, the alliance's progress and the doings of everyone who comes to him.
The Record Keeper is absent-minded, hard to get a straight answer from, and won't let anyone look through his pages uninvited.
The Record Keeper calls adventurers Aspirant and says the records watch them with great interest.
The Record Keeper admits the alliance is struggling to hold off everything coming for the archive.
The Record Keeper and his apprentice belong to Crux Eqal.
The wizard apprentice is the Record Keeper's apprentice and a wizard as well, two quite separate things.
The wizard apprentice studies how the archive changes its surroundings, chiefly the big crystals in the lobby, which collect the archive's stray magic.
Strike the lobby crystals and stray magic sometimes gathers into a sprite, neither solid, liquid nor gas, which turns to crystal the moment anyone notices it.
The archive's roots try to keep the crystals bound and pull back once the crystals are broken down; the wizard apprentice wants to know if the roots can think.
The wizard apprentice has no use for the mined rocks and tells miners to keep them, since they're thick with magic.
The druids in the archive's lobby are Crux Eqal; they love nature and will fight to defend it.
Temple Knights are posted in the archive's lobby with the rest of the alliance.
The alliance builders are bridging the great ravine through the middle of the lobby and putting up the camp and its defences.
One alliance builder brags his bridge will hold a thousand marching soldiers, and another tells him to stop boasting and get on with it.
An army needs more than soldiers, and the alliance builders are the rest of it.
The alliance's quartermaster is Liam, who no longer fights but supplies those who do, and he only reaches the raiders after their third fight.
The quartermaster's stock of brews, restores, prayer potions and fish runs low quickly, and there's sometimes a bowl of congealed leftovers in it.
Eva Cashien, niece of Sir Tiffy Cashien, leads the Temple Knights in the alliance, though she wears only plain White Knight armour.
Eva bears Guthix no grudge: she says Saradominists are bound to their god by faith, not his presence, and wishes people judged each follower on their own.
Eva thinks the archive's old magic is too unpredictable for anyone, and that Guthix did well to seal it away.
Eva says the defence is barely holding, the Temple Knights alone could never have held it, and the forces of evil caught everyone unprepared.
Armacus Selles is a high-ranking Guardian of Armadyl, a hearty old warrior fond of a joke, who leads the Guardians in the alliance.
Armacus thinks Guthix sending the gods away drove out as much justice as evil, but he stands with the alliance because its aims serve the justice he seeks.
Armacus reckons evil is the one on the back foot: the world is attacked without end and goodness still stands.
Armacus has wondered aloud whether defending the archive makes the alliance worthy of wielding its power, if only to defend it.
Ivy Sophista, a high-ranking druid of Crux Eqal, called the adventurer down to help hold the archive.
Ivy won't have the archive buried: she believes Guthix meant it to open one day, when the world was ready, and for now it must be guarded.
Ivy wishes the alliance leaned less towards order and justice, and would even take the Dagon'hai as wary allies now they've turned on Lucien.
Ivy likens the archive's artefacts to fire: dangerous, but useful once learned slowly and carefully.
Alliance Navigators guide the raiders on through the archive from one fight to the next.
Guardians of Armadyl in the archive call out that more potions are on the way.
The Record Keeper keeps the records of how the alliance is getting on.
The Record Keeper's apprentice is a young wizard.
The archive's banker loves nature, and reading.
The quartermaster manages the alliance's supplies.
The adventurer who helped the alliance came back out of the inner vault having faced Ocellus there, a Guthixian who opposed them with a shattered sword, and told the alliance's leaders he was dead.
The archive's reward chests hold, among other things, Zorya's tome, the rondache, the Ascension crossbows and the Obligator.
